investigation.title: Remote Agent Creation Failing: Kubernetes kata.peerpods.io/vm Resource Exhausted Across All Checks
investigation.summary: All three remote-agents eval checks (remote-agent-create, remote-agent-state, remote-agent-runtime) failed in production-api with identical Kubernetes scheduling errors: the cluster's 6 nodes have zero schedulable capacity for kata.peerpods.io/vm pods, with 2 nodes reporting insufficient kata.peerpods.io/vm resources and 4 nodes failing pod affinity/selector matching. Because the agent pod never scheduled, the eval runner never reached the createAgent call and produced no evidence, causing a total contract gap for all four required fields (orgId, agentId, vmIdPresent, remoteState).
investigation.rootCause: The Kubernetes cluster backing the remote-agents feature in production-api has exhausted its kata.peerpods.io/vm resource quota on the 2 nodes that carry that resource type. No preemption victims were available, so incoming agent pods remained Unschedulable for 131–146 seconds before the eval timed out. This is an infrastructure-layer scheduling failure, not an application code defect. The eval failure is a direct reflection of this cluster-level resource exhaustion. No evidence of a user-traffic or production incident signal is present in the packet; this is an observability eval failure that indicates the remote-agents provisioning path is currently non-functional in the production-api environment.

possibleCauses: PRIMARY — kata.peerpods.io/vm resource quota exhausted on the 2 eligible nodes in the production-api cluster: all available VM slots are occupied by existing pods and no preemption is configured or possible, leaving zero capacity for new agent pods.

SECONDARY — Node affinity/selector mismatch on the remaining 4 nodes: those nodes do not carry the kata.peerpods.io/vm extended resource or do not match the pod's required node selector, meaning the schedulable pool is structurally limited to 2 nodes regardless of overall cluster size.
TERTIARY — A cluster autoscaler or node pool scale-out is not configured or is not triggering for kata.peerpods.io/vm workloads, so the resource exhaustion is not self-healing.

LOWER CONFIDENCE — A recent change to pod resource requests or node affinity rules in the agent provisioning path could have increased per-pod resource consumption or narrowed the eligible node set, but no suspect changes are present in sourceDiscovery.suspectChanges to support this hypothesis.

investigation.title: Remote Agents: All Three Checks Failing Due to Exhausted kata.peerpods.io/vm Capacity on Production Kubernetes Cluster
investigation.summary: All three remote-agents eval checks (remote-agent-create, remote-agent-state, remote-agent-runtime) failed in the production-api environment at 2026-06-20T14:33–14:38Z with an identical Kubernetes scheduling error: the cluster's 6 nodes could not schedule the requested peer-pod VM because 2 nodes with kata.peerpods.io/vm capacity were fully exhausted and the remaining 4 nodes did not match the pod's node affinity/selector. Because the agent pod never became schedulable, the eval runner's createAgent call in run-status-probes.mjs never returned a live agent, and consequently no evidence (orgId, agentId, readyState, state) was written, causing the remote-agent-state expected-output contract to be entirely unmet.
investigation.rootCause: The Kubernetes cluster backing the production-api remote-agent swarm has exhausted its kata.peerpods.io/vm resource quota across the 2 eligible nodes. No preemption victims were available, and the 4 remaining nodes do not satisfy the pod's node affinity/selector. As a result, every remote-agent pod submitted during this eval window was stuck Unschedulable for ~130–148 seconds before the eval timed out. This is an infrastructure-layer scheduling failure, not an application code defect. The eval failure is a direct and accurate signal of this capacity constraint; no evidence of a user-traffic or production incident signal is present in the packet, so impact is scoped to the observability eval at this time.

Because no pod was ever scheduled, the agent VM was never provisioned, and the eval runner received no response evidence whatsoever — all five required contract fields (orgId, agentId, model, provider, message) are absent.
investigation.rootCause: The Kubernetes cluster backing the production-api remote-agent runtime has exhausted its kata.peerpods.io/vm extended resource on the 2 nodes that match the pod's affinity/selector. The scheduler reports 0/6 nodes available: 2 with insufficient kata.peerpods.io/vm capacity and 4 that do not match the pod's node affinity/selector at all. Preemption cannot help because no lower-priority victims exist on the eligible nodes. This is a cluster-level infrastructure constraint, not an eval configuration or code defect. The failure is localized to the remote-agents feature in production-api and is confirmed as an eval-layer failure; no user-traffic or incident signals are present in the supplied evidence.

investigations.title: Remote Agent Creation Failing: Kubernetes kata.peerpods.io/vm Resource Exhausted Across All Checks
investigations.summary: All three remote-agents eval checks (remote-agent-create, remote-agent-state, remote-agent-runtime) failed in production-api with identical Kubernetes scheduling errors: the cluster's 6 nodes have zero schedulable capacity for kata.peerpods.io/vm pods, with 2 nodes reporting insufficient kata.peerpods.io/vm resources and 4 nodes failing pod affinity/selector matching. Because the agent pod never scheduled, the eval runner never reached the createAgent call and produced no evidence, causing a total contract gap for all four required fields (orgId, agentId, vmIdPresent, remoteState).
investigations.rootCause: The Kubernetes cluster backing the remote-agents feature in production-api has exhausted its kata.peerpods.io/vm resource quota on the 2 nodes that carry that resource type. No preemption victims were available, so incoming agent pods remained Unschedulable for 131–146 seconds before the eval timed out. This is an infrastructure-layer scheduling failure, not an application code defect. The eval failure is a direct reflection of this cluster-level resource exhaustion. No evidence of a user-traffic or production incident signal is present in the packet; this is an observability eval failure that indicates the remote-agents provisioning path is currently non-functional in the production-api environment.

possibleCauses: PRIMARY — kata.peerpods.io/vm resource quota exhausted on the 2 eligible nodes in the production-api cluster: all available VM slots are occupied by existing pods and no preemption is configured or possible, leaving zero capacity for new agent pods.

SECONDARY — Node affinity/selector mismatch on the remaining 4 nodes: those nodes do not carry the kata.peerpods.io/vm extended resource or do not match the pod's required node selector, meaning the schedulable pool is structurally limited to 2 nodes regardless of overall cluster size.
TERTIARY — A cluster autoscaler or node pool scale-out is not configured or is not triggering for kata.peerpods.io/vm workloads, so the resource exhaustion is not self-healing.

LOWER CONFIDENCE — A recent change to pod resource requests or node affinity rules in the agent provisioning path could have increased per-pod resource consumption or narrowed the eligible node set, but no suspect changes are present in sourceDiscovery.suspectChanges to support this hypothesis.

If kubectl shows kata.peerpods.io/vm allocatable capacity is non-zero and no pods are consuming it on the affinity-eligible nodes, the root cause is not resource exhaustion but rather a different scheduling constraint (e.g., a changed affinity rule, taint, or resource request in the pod spec).

If the 4 non-matching nodes are found to have been recently removed from the eligible node pool (e.g., via a label or taint change), the affinity mismatch — not VM exhaustion — would be the primary cause.
If the eval runner logs show the pod was scheduled but the agent process itself failed to start or return a response, the root cause would shift from scheduling to agent runtime initialization.

Add a node-affinity-coverage eval that verifies the number of nodes matching the remote-agent pod's affinity/selector is above a minimum threshold, alerting before capacity is fully exhausted.
Add a pod-cleanup eval or teardown assertion that confirms eval-created remote-agent pods are fully terminated and their kata.peerpods.io/vm slots released after each run, to detect slot leaks early.

Consider a dedicated eval for the kata.peerpods.io/vm resource pool health that runs independently of the agent lifecycle checks, so scheduling infrastructure failures are distinguishable from agent software failures in the eval report.
